clue.text: Ray, hugging daughter, left in state of great confusion

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap your arms round, so one piece wraps round the others

blocks.note: a beam is a ray of light
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A man called Ray holds his daughter's hand and walks off, leaving everyone bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name, but it is a shaft of light that opens up to hold the two single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from the old London asylum of Bethlehem, is a common word for uproar and chaotic disorder.

clue.text: Male animal given fabulous fruit

blocks.note: a bull is the male of cattle
ace is slang for excellent or fabulous

explanation.surface: A beast is fed some wonderful, perhaps mythical, fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' suggests a fable, but here it simply means terrific. The answer is an uncommon word, so the wordplay does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullace is a wild plum, a small dark fruit related to the damson, found in British hedgerows.

clue.text: Defeated finally over issue? Resign

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept
in a down entry, one part placed over another sits above it in the column

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
to emit is to issue or give out

explanation.surface: After losing on some issue, a politician is urged to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a noun, a matter in dispute, but it is the verb meaning to send out.
explanation.definitionFit: Demit is a rather formal verb for giving up an office or position, the same as stepping down from a post.

clue.text: Slander from venomous creature, Irish

blocks.note: the asp is a venomous snake
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: Nasty gossip comes from a poisonous Irish snake of a person.
explanation.walkthrough: Slander here is a verb, matching the verb in the grid; Erse is a crossword favourite for Irish Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse someone is to attack their reputation with damaging false claims, a formal synonym for defaming them.

clue.text: Suit with things that get left in garden sheds

definitions.text: things that get left in garden sheds

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of cards

blocks.clueFragment: things that get left in garden sheds
blocks.note: second meaning: digging tools stored with the gardening kit

explanation.surface: Someone in a smart suit is surrounded by tools stored in garden sheds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests clothing, but it is the card suit; the long second half describes the garden tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a black card suit marked with pointed leaf symbols and the flat-bladed tools used for digging soil.

clue.text: US author twitching, using words rhythmically?

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: An American writer, nervously twitching, speaks in a sing-song rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitching' looks like a verb describing the author, but it stands for the noun for a nervous spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse uses metre and rhythm, so language with a measured rhythmic flow can be described as being like poetry.

clue.text: Criminal with ridiculous speed on dodgy road

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and out of order, so these letters are jumbled
dodgy means unreliable or faulty, so these letters are not to be taken in their given order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker drives at a crazy speed along a dangerous road.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams sit side by side, each with its own signal word, joined by 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, the bandit of Westerns, so a fair synonym for a criminal.

clue.text: Supporter of poor sons losing love, abandoned

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter is dropped
abandoned suggests wild and unrestrained behaviour, so the remaining letters run riot

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is nil in tennis, and O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A backer of poor boys has fallen out of love and been left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one O out of the eight letters, then rearrange the seven that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor backs a person or event with money, so the word is a straightforward synonym for a financial backer.

clue.text: True comedians performing in factual TV programmes

indicators.note: performers act out a routine, putting these letters through their paces into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Real comics appear in non-fiction television shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal sits between fodder and definition, reading naturally as comedians doing their act.
explanation.definitionFit: Documentaries are films or broadcasts presenting real events and people, the non-fiction strand of television.

clue.text: Some Paris luminaries in poor part of city

indicators.note: some means a portion only, so just a run of letters from inside the phrase is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Some famous Parisians are found living in a rundown district.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words: the last letter of the city and the first three of the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum is a squalid, overcrowded urban area where the poorest residents live, which matches a deprived district.

clue.text: Professional meeting reported in March

indicators.note: a report is something told by word of mouth, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: PRO is short for professional
a session is a meeting; cession, a giving up, is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A professional gathering takes place during the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' at the start of a word looks like the month, but it is a parade; capitals in clues can always be misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession is a body of people moving forward in orderly file, the same as a march or parade.

clue.text: Repartee from British worker meeting royal lady

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
the worker ant is a crossword favourite
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A British labourer exchanges witty remarks with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher and a common crossword stand-in for a royal lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee and banter both mean quick, playful exchanges of teasing remarks in conversation.

clue.text: Eve's ruin wrecked absolutely everything

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so these letters are broken and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Eve's downfall in Eden ruined the whole of creation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Fall in Genesis, where Eve's sin spoiled the world; the apostrophe is ignored in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is the totality of all existing matter, space and time, so it is everything there is.

clue.text: One who deals with a hive of activity

definitions.text: One who deals with a hive of activity

blocks.clueFragment: One who deals with a hive of activity
blocks.note: surface reading: a busy manager handling a bustling workplace
setter's reading: a literal hive full of busy insects

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hive of activity' is an idiom for a busy place, but here the hive is real and the activity is the honey makers'.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiarist tends colonies of honey bees, managing the hives and collecting their honey.

clue.text: King at this time, one unbelievable person not really so clever?

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
now means at this time
I is the Roman numeral one
a tall story is an unbelievable one

explanation.surface: A monarch today is an incredible figure, though perhaps not as bright as thought.
explanation.walkthrough: TALL for unbelievable comes from the phrase tall tale or tall story. The question mark marks a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-it-all behaves as though they understand everything, though the pose of superior intelligence is often unjustified.

clue.text: Loud tune in entertainment event

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A blaring tune is played at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: F is forte from musical notation; 'in' is a link joining wordplay to definition, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair is a travelling funfair or fete with rides, stalls and games, an outdoor gathering for amusement.

clue.text: Support the old man — it's right to get stuck in

indicators.note: getting stuck in means being lodged inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: pop is an informal word for father, often called the old man
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Help your elderly father: it is the proper thing to roll your sleeves up and get stuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stuck in' is British slang for getting on with a job enthusiastically, but here it means being inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a support holding something up, and to prop is to support it, so noun and verb both fit.

clue.text: Lady journalists covering extreme parts of empire

indicators.note: a cover goes all round, so one piece encloses another
extremes are the furthest points at either end, so the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the press is journalists collectively
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A noblewoman is pursued by reporters covering the far reaches of the empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' suggests reporting news, which suits journalists, but it means wrapping round.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress is a woman holding a rank in the peerage, so she is entitled to be addressed as Lady.

clue.text: Excellent group of directors? Right!

blocks.note: star as an adjective means outstanding
a company's directors sit on its board

explanation.surface: Someone praises an outstanding set of company directors and shouts in agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right!' reads as an exclamation of approval, but it is the direction on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the nautical term for the right-hand side of a vessel when facing forward towards the bow.

clue.text: Told to be independent? No

definitions.note: a phrase meaning the opposite of independent, so an adjective like the answer

blocks.note: first meaning: recounted, as a story is told
second meaning: not independent, connected to something else

explanation.surface: Someone is ordered to stand on their own two feet and refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like an instruction and a refusal; the 'No' turns independent into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Related means both recounted, as in a narrative, and connected or linked, which is the reverse of standing apart.

clue.text: Regret that could make me sorer

indicators.note: to make something from materials is to build it anew, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone worries that feeling sorry will only make them hurt more.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a near-sentence about pain; the fodder is unusually short and plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret or guilt for a wrong you have done, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Combined fighting force starts to experience difficulties

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: a unit is a body of troops
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A joint military force begins to run into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combined' looks like it describes the fighting force, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: United means joined together into a single whole, the same as combined or brought into union.

clue.text: Bishop, say — private individual needing more experience

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
e.g., for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
inner means private, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: A churchman, perhaps, is a private person who still has much to learn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private individual' wants to be read together, as a soldier or a recluse; it splits, with 'individual' starting the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is a novice who has only just started, so they lack practice and still have a lot to learn.

clue.text: Plant with sticky substance placed in shelter

indicators.note: to place one thing in another is to set it inside

blocks.note: gum is a sticky substance
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A gardener puts a sticky-sapped plant inside a greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee, the side out of the wind, is a common crossword word for shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A legume is any plant of the pea family, such as beans, peas and lentils, bearing seeds in pods.

clue.text: Solemn girl's first to have wild party!

indicators.note: first means the very beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a rave is a wild party

explanation.surface: A serious young woman is the first to throw a wild party, which is surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark plays on the contrast between a serious girl and a riotous party.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave describes a serious, dignified manner, the same as solemn in tone or bearing.

clue.text: Leave fellows needing time in division of company

blocks.note: to depart is to leave
fellows are men
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Staff ask for time off from work in one section of the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' suggests holiday time off work, but it is the verb meaning go away.
explanation.definitionFit: A department is a section of an organisation responsible for one area of its work, like sales or accounts.

clue.text: Excellent railway, well ventilated

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A fine railway carriage is pleasantly breezy.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, top quality, appears as AI in crosswords since the digit 1 resembles the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room has plenty of fresh air circulating through it, the same as one that is well ventilated.

clue.text: South Africa has boys making healthy dishes

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
lads are boys

explanation.surface: In South Africa, young men are preparing nutritious food.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are standard: the country abbreviation and a British word for young men.
explanation.definitionFit: Salads are cold dishes of raw vegetables and leaves, widely thought of as wholesome, nutritious food.

clue.text: Stick notice on front of present

blocks.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
here means present, as at a roll call

explanation.surface: Someone sticks a label on the front of a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but it is the adjective, as in answering a register.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface, the same as glue holding something in place.
